title: Egg omelet or scrambled egg with cheese, made with animal fat or meat drippings (1983)

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of eggs, cheese, and animal fat (such as butter, lard, or meat drippings). Eggs are beaten and cooked in a pan with the fat, then grated cheese is folded in. This preparation is typical of traditional cuisines where animal fats were readily available.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are one of the oldest foods known to humanity.
The cheese can range from soft cottage cheese to hard cheddar.
Animal fat enhances flavor and aroma but also raises the calorie count.
In 1983 this dish was commonly served in cafeterias and home kitchens as a quick, hearty breakfast.
Traditionally omelets were cooked in cast‑iron skillets, which provided even heat distribution.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs and cheese provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamins D and B12
items.content: Animal fat and eggs contain vitamin D, while cheese supplies vitamin B12, both important for nervous system function and blood formation.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: The dish supplies calcium from cheese and phosphorus from eggs, supporting bone health.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: Fat offers a quick source of energy, useful during periods of high physical activity.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Cooking with animal fat increases saturated fat levels, which may affect cholesterol when consumed frequently.

items.title: Allergy to eggs or dairy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs or cheese.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The dish is relatively high in calories; portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑managed diets.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol, so people with elevated cholesterol should limit intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beat the eggs, season with salt and pepper, heat a pan with a small amount of animal fat, pour in the eggs, and when they begin to set, sprinkle grated cheese and continue cooking to the desired doneness. Serve hot, optionally garnished with herbs or vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The omelet is best eaten fresh. If needed, store in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours in an airtight container. Reheat in a pan or microwave, adding a little fat to prevent drying out.
